q: 1. Tacheometric formula for horizontal distance using horizontal sights can also suitable be employed for inclined sights through θ by multiplying ...............
options: the multiplying constant by cos²θ and additive constant by cos θ
explain: The standard horizontal distance formula for inclined sights is D = ks cos²θ + c cosθ.

q: 2. Back bearing of a line is equal to ...............
explain: Back Bearing = Fore Bearing ± 180° (use + if FB < 180°, and - if FB > 180°).

q: 3. The magnetic bearing of a line is 32° and the magnetic declination is 10°15'W. The true bearing is ...............
explain: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - West Declination = 32°00' - 10°15' = 21°45'.

q: 4. θ1 and θ2 are the angles of elevation from A to the top and bottom of vertically held rod of length S at B. The horizontal distance AB is ...............
explain: Using trigonometry: h1 = D tan θ1 and h2 = D tan θ2. The length S = h1 - h2 = D(tan θ1 - tan θ2), so D = S/(tan θ1 - tan θ2).

q: 5. In precision theodolite traverse... the angular error of closure should not exceed
explain: For standard/ordinary traversing, the error is often capped at $1' \sqrt{N}$, where N is the number of stations.

q: 6. The projection of a traverse line on a line parallel to the meridian is known as
explain: Latitude is the projection of a line on the North-South axis (parallel to the meridian).

q: 7. In measuring horizontal angles, the theodolite should be turned
options: clockwise from the forward station to the back station
clockwise from the back station to the forward station
anticlockwise from the back station to the forward station
anticlockwise from the forward station to the back station
explain: Standard practice for measuring horizontal angles with a theodolite is to sight the back station, set the scale, and then turn the instrument clockwise to the forward station.

q: 8. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 120°, its quadrant bearing is
explain: 120° lies in the second quadrant (SE). Quadrant Bearing = $180 - 120 = 60°$. Thus, S 60° E.

q: 9. In any closed traverse, if they survey work is correct, then .............
options: the algebraic sum of latitudes should be equal to zero
the algebraic sum of departures should be equal to zero
the sum of northings should be equal to the sum of southings
explain: For a closed traverse, the sum of latitudes (Northings - Southings) and departures (Eastings - Westings) must both equal zero.

q: 10. Right face and left reading are taken to .............
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation
explain: Changing the face of the theodolite (Face Left and Face Right) eliminates errors due to the line of collimation not being perpendicular to the trunnion axis and the trunnion axis not being perpendicular to the vertical axis.

q: 11. When the angular and linear measurements are equally precise in traversing, the balancing of a traverse is done by .............
explain: Bowditch's rule (Compass Rule) is used when linear and angular measurements are of equal precision. It assumes errors in linear measurements are proportional to √L.

q: 12. A deflection angle in a traverse is equal to the .............
options: difference between the included angle and 180°
difference between 360° and the included angle and 180°
sum of the included angel and 180°
explain: In any traverse, the deflection angle at a station is 180° minus the internal included angle (or included angle - 180° for external).

q: 13. The branch of surveying in which both horizontal and vertical positions of a point, are determined by making in instrumental observations, is known .............
explain: Tacheometry is a branch of angular surveying in which horizontal and vertical distances are determined by optical observations on a staff, eliminating chaining.

q: 14. If L is the specified length of a tape, L1 its actual length and S the measured distance, then the true distance is given by the formula .............
explain: True Distance = (Actual Length / Nominal Length) x Measured Distance. If the tape is longer than specified, the recorded distance is too short, and vice versa.

q: 15. In a quadrantal system, the bearing of a line is measured
options: clockwise or anticlockwise from North/South whichever is nearer...
explain: In the Reduced Bearing (RB) or Quadrantal system, bearings are measured from either North or South towards East or West, whichever is closer, ranging from 0° to 90°.

q: 16. In a whole circle bearing system N25°15'W corresponds to
explain: To convert N 25°15' W to WCB: 360° - 25°15' = 334°45' (since the bearing is in the 4th quadrant).

q: 17. If the fore bearing of a line is 36°15', its back bearing will be
explain: Back Bearing = Fore Bearing ± 180°. Since 36°15' is less than 180°, we add 180°: 36°15' + 180° = 216°15'.

q: 18. If the fore bearing of a line is N26°35'W, its back bearing will be
explain: In the Quadrantal system, the back bearing has the same numerical value but opposite cardinal directions (N becomes S, W becomes E).

q: 19. In tacheometrical observations, vertical staff holding is generally preferred to normal staffing, due to
options: minimum effect of careless holding on the result
explain: Holding the staff vertically is easier for the staff-man and results in smaller errors if the staff is slightly out of plumb compared to trying to hold it normal (perpendicular) to the line of sight.

q: 20. In tangential tacheometry, an ordinary level staff is used
explain: Tangential tacheometry calculations assume the staff is held perfectly vertical so that the tangent values of the observed vertical angles can be applied.

q: 21. Horizontal distances obtained tacheometrically are corrected for
explain: For very long sights, tacheometric readings must be corrected for the earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction, which affect the perceived staff intercept.

q: 22. Magnetic bearing of a survey line at any place
options: is always greater than true bearing
explain: Because of annual and secular variations in magnetic declination, the magnetic bearing of a fixed line will change over the months and years.

q: 23. The distance between terminal points computed from known, as
explain: A traverse base is a line whose length and direction are precisely known or calculated to serve as a reference for the rest of the survey network.

q: 24. To avoid large centering error with very short legs, observations are generally made
options: to a target fixed on theodolite tripod
explain: When traverse legs are short, even a small displacement in centering causes a large angular error. Using high-precision optical plummet systems and fixed targets minimizes this risk.

q: 25. The lines passing through points at which the magnetic declination is equal at a given time are called .............
explain: Isogonic lines connect points of equal magnetic declination. Agonic lines connect points of zero declination.

q: 26. When internal angles are to be subtended by a theodolite survey for closed traverse .............
options: exterior angles are measures when the traverse goes anti-clockwise
explain: In a closed traverse, running counter-clockwise results in the measurement of interior angles when observing angles to the right.

q: 27. For a closed traverse the omitted measurements may be calculated .............
options: length or bearing of adjacent side
explain: In a closed traverse, if $\sum Latitude = 0$ and $\sum Departure = 0$, you can solve for up to two unknown quantities (like one length and one bearing, or two lengths).

q: 28. The length of a traverse line (L) may be obtained by .............
explain: All three formulas are mathematically valid based on the geometry of coordinates and bearings ($Lat = L \cos \theta$, $Dep = L \sin \theta$).

q: 29. While rotating the theodolite in the horizontal plane, the bubble of the bubble tube takes up the same position in its tube, it indicates .............
options: the line of collimation is perpendicular to vertical axis
explain: If the bubble remains centered throughout a 360-degree rotation, it confirms the vertical axis of the instrument is truly vertical.

q: 30. The multiplying constant for the tacheometer is .............
explain: The multiplying constant is denoted by $k = f/i$, where $f$ is focal length and $i$ is stadia interval.

q: 31. The additive constant for the tacheometer is .............
explain: The additive constant is denoted by $C = f + d$, where $d$ is the distance from the objective to the vertical axis.

q: 32. The variation of magnetic declination within a day is called .............
explain: Diurnal variation refers to the systematic changes in magnetic declination that occur over a 24-hour period, typically influenced by the sun's position.
